যে গানে জীবন ও ইতিহাস কথা বলে: সাধক হালি: Songs where life and history speak: a tribute to Sadhak Halim Boyati
কিছু শিল্পীর কণ্ঠ থেমে গেলেও তাঁদের গান: Even when some artists’ voices fall silent, their songs live on in people’s mouths, their disciples’ memories, and gatherings rooted in the soil.
সাধক হালিম বয়াতি—আবদুল হালিম মিয়া—ছিলেন: Sadhak Halim Boyati—Abdul Halim Mia—was one such artist. His songs and performances brought together currents of jari, bichar songs, sarinda, and spiritual reflection. This tribute draws on music, memories, and verifiable information.

জারি গানের আসরে এক শিল্পী ও পথপ্রদর্শক: An artist and guide in the jari gathering
লোকগানের আসর ছিল হালিম বয়াতির শিল্পীজীবন: Folk-music gatherings were at the heart of Halim Boyati’s artistic life. A jari troupe leader, or boyati, does more than sing: he carries the story, melody, rhythm, dialogue, and ensemble performance forward together. A documentary by Dr Simon Zakaria presents Abdul Helim Boyati as an important artist, playwright, and director of bishad-jari. It tells the story of his development as an artist and explores the features of jari song and dance. The filmmaker’s description states that his training and initiatives helped preserve the jari and jari-dance traditions of the Netrokona region.

বিচার গানে যুক্তি, সুর ও সাধনা: Reason, melody, and spiritual practice in bichar songs
বিচার গান কথার লড়াইকে সুরের ভাষায় মঞ্চে: Bichar songs bring verbal debate to the stage through music. Performers take turns in song and speech to create space for questions, responses, argument, and reflection. Ethnomusicologist Bertie Moontasir Kibreah’s University of Chicago dissertation discusses Halim Boyati as one of the influential boyati artists of the twentieth century. The research includes interviews and fieldwork on his performances, songwriting, relationships with disciples, and the setting of Sufi practice.
বাংলাদেশ সংবাদ সংস্থা জানিয়েছে, তাঁর রচি: Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha reports that his more than five thousand songs are known as “Halim Sangeet”; their subjects included the body, sharia, marfat, haqiqat, tariqat, and patriotism. He participated in the 1971 Liberation War and received an honorary fellowship from Bangla Academy in 2001. His songs are therefore more than musical richness: they are also records of the ideas, beliefs, and human experiences of a time.
সারিন্দার সুরে তাঁর অবদান: His contribution to the sound of the sarinda
হালিম বয়াতির নাম সারিন্দার সঙ্গেও গভীরভা: Halim Boyati’s name is deeply associated with the sarinda. By playing it in a live radio programme in 1957, he played an important role in bringing the instrument to a wider audience. However, he did not invent the sarinda: a biographical article in Samakal states that rural musicians had played it before him. His particular contribution was bringing its sound to urban and distant listeners through radio.
সারিন্দার স্বতন্ত্র ধ্বনি বহু ধারার লোকস: The sarinda’s distinctive sound has been used in many folk-music traditions. The Daily Star’s discussion of the instrument notes its use in Baul, Sufi-marfati, and sadhak music. Its cultural history therefore does not belong to a single artist; Halim Boyati’s contribution is a memorable chapter in that long tradition.
গান থেকে মানুষ, মানুষ থেকে উত্তরাধিকার: From songs to people, from people to a legacy
ঢাকা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের টিএসসি চত্বরে ২০২৬: At a 2026 memorial gathering at Dhaka University’s TSC, his son Nishane Halim and disciples shared memories alongside performances of his songs. Samakal reports that many aspects of his life and work have yet to be fully documented; collecting oral histories from family members, disciples, intellectual followers, and fellow musicians is urgent. This call matters to us too: recordings of his voice, song notebooks, performance videos, disciples’ memories, and family documents all need preservation.
সামাজিক মাধ্যমে তাঁর সারিন্দা পাওয়ার একট: A story of a miraculous event in which he acquired his sarinda has circulated on social media. Such devotional memories may be meaningful to people. However, the news, research, and documentary sources we found do not independently confirm this particular event. With respect, it should therefore be identified as oral or spiritual memory rather than verified biographical fact. Interviews with family members, disciples, or eyewitnesses could help preserve the memory’s origins and context more carefully.
সাধক হালিম বয়াতিকে স্মরণ মানে তাঁর গান শ: Remembering Sadhak Halim Boyati means listening to his songs, learning from his disciples, respecting gatherings of jari and bichar songs, and working to pass this tradition to future generations. Building a fuller record of his life and creative work could be our living tribute to him.
